newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits fall 3.4 pct in September.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits fall 3.4 pct in September.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in September fell 3.4 percent to C$2.07 billion, seasonally adjusted, from August, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 3.6 percent after a 8.9 percent fall in August.
Statistics Canada said the value of building permits issued in the third quarter rose 2.8 percent to C$6.62 billion from C$6.44 billion in the second quarter.
The agency said this was the third straight quarterly increase in building permits after six quarters of declines.
"As a result of better affordability in housing and exceptionally low mortgage rates, the short-term outlook for new housing construction remains positive," the federal government agency said.
Over the first nine months of 1996 the value of residential building permits rose 14.3 percent from the same period in 1995.
Non-residential construction intentions rose 5.2 percent in the third quarter to C$2.8 billion, led by the industrial and commercial sectors.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
